newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midcontinent diesel fuel differentials ease.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midcontinent diesel fuel differentials ease.

text.p: U.S. Midcontinent diesel fuel prices eased modestly late Tuesday on lower differentials from weak demand despite a draw in distillate stocks in the region, traders said.

Distillate inventories were drawn down 287,000 barrels in the PADD II, Midwest refining region but remained 182,000 barrels above last-year's levels, the American Petroleum Institute reported late in the day.
Gasoline differentials were steady in Chicago and Group Three following the trade group's report of a 160,000 barrel draw in gasoline stocks, traders said.
Group Three low sulphur diesel eased to bids even with the print for prompt deliveries and 0.50 cent under for later deliveries. High sulphur remained 2.0/1.75 cents under.

Chicago low sulphur diesel was talked 2.0/1.75 cents a gallon under the print for October deliveries, with high sulphur remaining 3.75 cents under the print after plunging in early morning discussion.
Group Three unleaded remained 1.00/0.75 cent a gallon under the print for prompt deliveries and 1.25/1.0 cent under for later deliveries, with premium steady at 2.50 cents higher.
Chicago prompt October unleaded gasoline differentials were talked unchanged at 0.50/0.25 cent a gallon under the print, with later deliveries a cent weaker and premium 2.75 cents higher.
Jet/kero was talked 1.0/1.25 cents over the print in both markets.
